svg.aria-label: Upper panel: Rayleigh-Taylor growth rate against wavelength for water held above air, drawn twice, once with interfacial tension and once without. Without tension the rate rises without limit as the wavelength shortens. With tension it peaks at about three centimetres and falls to zero at 1.71 centimetres. Lower panel: Kelvin-Helmholtz growth rate against wavelength for the solar interface of the anchor observation, drawn twice, once with gravity acting across the interface and once without. Without gravity the rate rises steadily as the wavelength shortens; with gravity it falls to zero at about five thousand kilometres, which is shorter than the seven thousand kilometre wavelength that was observed.
svg.text: Rayleigh–Taylor: water held above air, with and without surface tension
Kelvin–Helmholtz on the CME flank: what gravity would do if it acted across the interface
gravity across it: cut off at 5124 km
ΔU = 20 km/s, ρ ratio 2.24, ne = 3×10⁸ cm⁻³
Solar inputs: Ofman & Thompson (2011), ApJ 734, L11. The coronal density is carried from Module 1 and is an input, not a measurement; the cutoff moves as ne⁰.
